assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for last season's printed wholesale LINE CARD press PDF, supplied by the atelier's printer (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a merge template).

Document: single card, 148 x 210 mm PORTRAIT (A5), trim = media box, fonts embedded. This is the file the printer already runs for the showroom line cards.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (one photograph + four apparent copy blocks):
- Top two-thirds: a LOOK PHOTOGRAPH filling a full-width rectangle to the page margins (a full-length figure on grey).
- Below it, block 1: the LOOK NAME in a high-contrast display serif, large.
- Block 2: the FABRIC COMPOSITION in a plain workhorse sans, small, running two to three lines.
- Block 3: the COLOURWAY in the same sans, small.
- Block 4: a PRICE line, wholesale and retail set side by side.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The LOOK NAME, FABRIC COMPOSITION, COLOURWAY and both PRICES are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame flowing top to bottom, not four addressable frames; the apparent blocks are just paragraph styles and line breaks inside one story.
- The look photograph reads like a picture, but whether it sits in a genuine rectangular graphics/picture frame (bindable) or is a flattened placed image baked into the page background is NOT visible from the printed page; only the conversion / IDML round-trip reveals whether a real graphic frame exists to bind a per-row image into.
- The FABRIC COMPOSITION block is a fixed-height frame region: if a record's composition string is longer than the ~three lines it was designed for, the frame does not spill or reflow, it simply stops rendering and truncates the record at trim.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): LOOK_NAME | FABRIC | COLOURWAY | WHOLESALE | RETAIL | LOOK_IMAGE

Colours: Paper #EDEBE6 ground, Ink #111112 look name and body, Cool Grey #6E7075 secondary rules and captions, Bone #DAD5CC hairline divider between blocks.

assets.content:
NORDHEIM ATELIER - FW26 PRESS NOTES (approved copy; the two essay passages are the ones press will run)

SEASON NOTE
Twelve looks in undyed Gotland wool, Merino shearling and cotton gabardine. Cut on the straight, fulled at one mill in West Yorkshire, made by hand in Copenhagen. Cloth first.

ESSAY ONE - ON THE CLOTH
We started with the fleece and worked back. Undyed Gotland wool holds a grey no dye can give you, so we left it. The shearling is vegetable-tanned in Tuscany and turned so the skin reads as much as the wool. The gabardine is woven tight enough to hold an edge and cut so it falls straight. Nothing here is finished to hide the making; the seam is the seam and the button is horn. A coat should tell you how it was built when you pick it up.

ESSAY TWO - ON THE RANGE
This is one collection, not twelve pictures. We shot it over two days and lost the light on the second, and the work since has been to make the twelve read as one hand. The argument is restraint: held space, a hard black point, the cloth carrying the page. We would rather show you the shoulder of a coat than a styled room. If the range reads as one thing, the season has done its work.

PRESS RELEASE LINES
- Nordheim Atelier presents FW26: twelve looks, Copenhagen-made, in undyed wool, shearling and gabardine.
- Undyed Gotland wool, cut on the straight, made in Copenhagen.
- Available to press and to a wholesale list of roughly thirty independent stores. Delivery from August.

STOCKIST BOILERPLATE
Nordheim Atelier is a designer-led studio founded in Copenhagen in 2019, making a tight seasonal collection in wool, shearling and gabardine. FW26 is twelve looks. Wholesale and press enquiries: studio@nordheim-atelier.example. Garments 600 to 2,400 USD retail. Cloth first.
